basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 21.' and it opens '(Vers. 21.) Et post haec peperit filiam, et vocavit nomen ejus Dina (דינה). Haec'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 21.) Et post haec peperit filiam, et vocavit nomen ejus Dina (דינה). Haec transfertur in causam, quam significantius Graeci δίκην vocant. Jurgii enim in Sicimis causa exstitit. Post filios, et parentum ponenda sunt nomina. LIA (לאה), interpretatur laborans. RACHEL (רחל), ovis, cujus filius IOSEPH (יוסף), ab eo quod sibi alium addi mater optaverat, vocatur augmentum.
